data.current_summary: Import files attached in an assistant's conversation
data.current_description:
In place of creating a session, uploading parts and completing each file, when the files are attached in a conversation with an assistant that gives your app a download link for each one, as ChatGPT does: creates the session, uploads every file (1 to 100) from its link and completes it, in one call. The session's limits apply, and every file needs one available credit. The links expire a few minutes after the assistant gives them. When any link cannot be read, nothing is created and nothing is charged.

Files are independent: one that cannot be uploaded carries its `error` and is listed in `failed_file_ids`, and the completed files can be submitted. A retry with the same `upload_session_id` and files continues the session, and a file already completed is not uploaded again.

Rate limit: 20 requests per minute per API key.
data.summary_suggestion: Upload files from assistant-provided links in one call
data.description_suggestion:
Streamlined alternative to the standard upload workflow: creates an upload session, downloads and uploads files (1 to 100) from assistant-provided links, and completes them in a single request. Each file requires one available credit. Links expire within minutes of being provided by the assistant.

Partial success is supported: files that cannot be downloaded are listed in `failed_file_ids` with error details, while successfully uploaded files can be submitted for extraction. Idempotent: retrying with the same `upload_session_id` and files continues the session without re-uploading already-completed files. No charges are incurred if all links fail.

Rate limit: 20 requests per minute per API key.

data.current_summary: Get the extracted rows as JSON
data.current_description:
The rows of a completed extraction, in pages, each row an object keyed by the output
columns exactly as the JSON output file holds it: native JSON types when the extraction
was submitted with `options.json_typed_values`, strings otherwise. The `Source File`
and `Review Needed` columns are present unless excluded at submission. The Review
Needed items whose rows fall on the page come back alongside; `review_needed.count` is
the count for the whole extraction. Rows are available for the same 90 days as the
output files.

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per API key.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve paginated extraction results as JSON
data.description_suggestion: Returns the structured rows from a completed extraction, paginated and formatted as JSON objects. Each row is keyed by output column names with values as native JSON types (if `options.json_typed_values` was set) or strings. Includes `Source File` and `Review Needed` columns unless excluded at submission. Returns associated `ReviewNeeded` items for rows on the requested page, with `review_needed.count` reflecting the total count across the entire extraction. Results are retained for 90 days from submission. Only available for completed extractions.

data.current_description:
The stable record of one extraction: the original prompt and options, every file name,
and the page-level results, prompt notes and Review Needed items of a completed one.
Unlike `getExtraction`, this endpoint always answers `success: true`; a failed
extraction is a valid record with its failure inside `error`. It carries no download
URLs; use `getOutputDownloadUrl` for those.

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per API key.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve complete extraction metadata and results
data.description_suggestion: Returns the complete extraction record including the original prompt, submission options, all source file names, and for completed extractions: page-level results, prompt notes (UncertaintyNote items), and Review Needed items. This endpoint always returns `success: true` even for failed extractions; failure details are included in the `error` field. Unlike `getExtraction`, this endpoint does not include download URLs; use `getOutputDownloadUrl` to obtain signed URLs for output files. Useful for auditing extraction configuration and reviewing all associated metadata.

data.current_summary: Answer the questions an extraction stopped to ask
data.current_description:
Answers open questions of an extraction whose status is `input_required`. Answer every
open question in one request or across several; the extraction continues the moment
every open question has an answer. The response is the extraction's status after the
answers, exactly as `getExtraction` returns it.

An answer governs the whole extraction, every document in it and not only the one in
the question's example; where the right answer differs by document type, say so in
`text`, which is accepted on every question. Your own words are screened before they are
used: an answer given in bad faith, one that tries to misuse the service rather than
answer the question, is refused and the question is asked again with
`previous_answer_rejected: true`; after three refused answers the extraction is
cancelled with `cancellation_reason: answers_rejected`. A vague or undecided answer is
not refused: it is applied, and the matter may be asked again as a new question.

An answer to a question that is no longer waiting changes nothing and returns the
current status, so a request can be repeated after a dropped connection. Only a request
that could never be right is refused, whole, with `INVALID_INPUT`.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute per API key.
data.summary_suggestion: Submit answers to extraction clarification questions
data.description_suggestion:
Provides answers to open questions from an extraction in `input_required` status. Answers can be submitted all at once or incrementally; the extraction resumes processing once all open questions are answered. Returns the extraction's updated status matching the `getExtraction` response format.

Key behaviors: (1) Each answer applies to the entire extraction across all documents, not just the example document in the question; (2) Answers are validated for good faith; rejected answers trigger `previous_answer_rejected: true` and after three rejections the extraction is cancelled with `cancellation_reason: answers_rejected`; (3) Vague or uncertain answers are accepted and may be re-asked as new questions; (4) Answers to questions no longer waiting are ignored and return current status (safe for retry after connection loss); (5) Only fundamentally invalid requests are rejected with `INVALID_INPUT`. For document-type-specific answers, include clarification in the `text` field.
